observation.visible_scene: A low sun, rendered as a bright white disc, sits directly on a flat ocean horizon beneath a smooth orange-to-red sky gradient. The foreground and midground are a dark, choppy sea with rolling swells, scattered white foam on breaking crests, and a vertical reddish reflection column glowing on the water just below the sun.
visible_changes: The sea surface is in continuous motion: wave crests and troughs rise, fall, and shift horizontally across the frame, and patches of white foam appear, break, and disappear at changing positions (e.g. foam at the lower-left in early frames, a foamy crest along the bottom in later frames).
The glinting white highlights on the wave tops and the reddish glow column beneath the sun flicker and move as the water undulates, rather than staying fixed.

The sun disc itself keeps an essentially constant vertical and horizontal position relative to the horizon throughout the excerpt; no clearly visible sinking, rising, or change in apparent size occurs within the sampled ~2.7 s.
The orange-red sky gradient and the horizon line remain stable in color and placement.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the sun is in fact setting (or rising) on a longer timescale; the crop is too short to show any measurable descent.
The net direction and period of the wave train over a longer interval.
Any context before t=0 or after the last frame.
uncertain_details: Tiny apparent vertical shifts of the sun/horizon between frames cannot be cleanly separated from minor handheld camera jitter, so camera motion is treated as uncertain/negligible.
Exact propagation direction of individual wave crests is hard to track frame-to-frame.
